title: European audiences and musicians
summary: Howard praises quiet attentive audiences, jam sessions, brass bands welcoming them in London, and the Copenhagen arrival.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I'm sure that Dick would like to know a little about how you find the European audience compared to the American audience, especially the audience here in New Orleans.
Well, they were wonderful, wonderful audiences.
You think they understand anything?

Well, I'm quite sure they did. They made sure that they were very quiet until things was, you do a number, they'll wait completely, until everything was over before they would applaud and let you know that they enjoyed.

Yeah. Yeah. Well, I think the European audience seems to me to be very serious about jazz music, but maybe it's interesting to go into the shop a little further. Did you have the feeling that they understood the background of the music, that they, did they applaud in the right places when you were playing nice and good?
Oh yeah, you could tell when they, you get to feel that feeling on them, you could tell, you could feel them.
Did you have a chance to listen to any of the European jazz bands?

Well, frankly all of them, because we were, we were to all the nice spots. The first one that we went to, when we arrived in Liverpool, we had to stay overnight, and I, I got kind of unconcerned about going on the ground. I had double band, this is what's thing is that, you know. And we've had a good many good musicians over there that night, we had a jam section.
They all wanted you to come and play with the band. Yeah, we did. We did.
In fact, every place we went. You enjoyed it?
We enjoyed it.
We enjoyed it. After the concert we would go down and join it with them and have a wonderful time.
What's the main difference, do you think, between the way the kids in Europe play your music and the way you play right here in New Orleans?

Well to my idea it's real good. That's all I could say about it. They play the tunes wonderfully and they play the same tune that we play. And in fact when we got to, when we arrived in London, the brass band, when we were getting off the train and I heard the brass band I couldn't believe my ears. They were playing the same, the song that we play is on the street and it was good.
I remember there was a brass band down receiving you almost in every city or right? Yeah, that's right.
The smallest group was the three pieces if you remember in Sweden and they still was out, the young fellow. I think it was saxophone, banjo, or something else. But anyway that was the smallest band.
In the morning you arrived at Copenhagen I think that was, you missed some train or something happened going to.

Well we came to Copenhagen but we couldn't come down due to the weather. So we had to go back into Hamsburg in Germany and we got the night train out and we arrived in Copenhagen that Sunday morning. At 6 o'clock.
Yeah. In the morning. And right away you had to go down and play I think in the entrance hall.
What about coming into London? I wanted to ask you what happened after, when you arrived in the train station in London.

Oh that's what I was speaking about. Kent's band, he had about a twenty piece brass band or something like that. And the song that they were playing sounded the same like the way we played. And they had people on top of the sheds and so forth. And I understood that a couple of them got away to, been caved in.
Well they had some people there. They did have some people. She said hey. Go ahead. I just want to know about that, that came in.
I see. Did you have an opportunity to, besides meeting the European musicians, to meet European fans of jazz and talk to them about the, do you feel they were very interested in the music?
Well yeah, we had quite a bit of people would come during the day and come up and talk.
Yeah.
About the, and we was interviewed quite a bit in London by reporters and so forth.
They wanted to get the message from you. Yeah. The message from you. That's right. Would you like to go to Europe again?
